title: Databases
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Design and use relational databases: the relational model and relational algebra, SQL queries with joins, grouping and subqueries, data definition, constraints and views, ER modeling and normalization, storage and indexes, query processing, transactions and isolation, recovery, and an overview of NoSQL and distributed databases.
primary_reading: CMU 15-445/645 Database Systems (free lectures and notes)

weeks.3: SQL: SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY
weeks.6: SQL: changing data, constraints and views
weeks.8: Normalization: functional dependencies and normal forms
weeks.9: Storage and indexes: B+ trees and hashing

blocks.deliverable: Write join queries on a supplied schema.
Week 7 midterm; normalize a schema to BCNF.
Choose indexes for a query workload.
Identify the anomalies each isolation level allows.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Design and build a database for supplied requirements: an ER diagram, a normalized schema, sample data, 15 SQL queries that answer stated questions, chosen indexes with reasons, and a Python program that uses the database through sqlite3.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
